findings.reason: The protected Python solution iterates through sorted unique elements nums while tracking next_missing starting at lower. When next_missing < value, it appends [next_missing, value - 1] to the output and sets next_missing = value + 1. After the loop, if next_missing <= upper, it appends [next_missing, upper]. The algorithm runs in O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space; no candidate is required.

Tracking a single next_missing pointer and advancing it across sorted array elements correctly identifies all missing ranges in inclusive bounds [lower, upper] without missing gaps or overlapping bounds.
Scanning nums takes O(n) time independent of numeric interval width. Auxiliary space is O(1) for scalar variables (excluding output list). Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts nums (List[int]), lower (int), upper (int), returning List[List[int]] representing missing ranges [a, b].

The approach accurately details frontier advancement across sorted values, range generation criteria, single-element range format [x, x], and O(n) time / O(1) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover full range scan performance traps, list membership linear overheads, set conversion space costs, integer overflow sentinel risks, empty array input, fully present array input, and missing prefix/suffix/singleton coverage.
